correctness.rationale: The parity lemma forces every finite length even. For q=1(mod4) the first remainder is 1/(qx). Otherwise x=(q+3)/2 and remainder 3/A (A=qx); the 3|A branch gives q=3(mod12) and two steps. For q=7,11(mod12), A=5(mod6), y=(A+4)/3 gives 4/D with D=Ay=7(mod8); z=(D+5)/4 gives 5/(Dz). The remaining unit fraction is attained iff 5|D, equivalently A=0 or 1(mod5); A=1 is impossible since q^2+3q-2 has discriminant 17=2(mod5), a nonsquare. CRT yields precisely four exactly-four-term classes, twenty two-term classes, and six remaining classes; compare shifts 12,20,30 from class7 to prove least even period. Independent fractions.Fraction recalculation checked all odd 3<=q<=2001 (667 length-two, 133 length-four, 200 still nonzero). These finite tests corroborate the all-q CRT proof, not substitute for it.
